### `lib/src/drafts.dart`

- **class `DraftWriteContext`** — The write policy of a change made below a form.
  - `const DraftWriteContext({required this.identity, required this.save})`
  - `final Object identity`
  - `final Future<Entity?> Function(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json) save` — Writes [json] over [entity] through the bound writer and answers the file it wrote, or null where it wrote none.
- **class `DraftWriteConflictException`** — A pending change belongs to a different bound writer.
  - `const DraftWriteConflictException()`
- **class `OpenDraft`** — A form's draft while its page is open.
  - `String get stem` — The stem of the file this is the draft of.
  - `String? get projectKey` — The film the form was built for; null only for unbound test seams.
  - `Future<bool> settle()` — Waits for a write in flight, then writes what is pending.
  - `Map<String, dynamic>? get pending` — **The whole document this draft would write** — the file as it was read with what is typed on top — while something is pending, and **null when nothing is**.
  - `Map<String, dynamic> get snapshot` — A deep copy of the current document, including a write in flight and newer typing.
  - `void adopt(Entity written)` — Takes the writer's hand-back of a write made from this draft as the base of its next write.
  - `Future<Object?> apply(void Function(Map<String, dynamic> draft) change, {String? key, bool reseed = false, DraftWriteContext? writeContext})` — Takes [change] as it takes a keystroke, and writes it now.
- **class `EditableDraft`** — An open draft a card below the forms edits as the page's own: it changes the draft as a keystroke does, and says when the draft changed, so that the card shows what the form shows.
  - `void change(void Function(Map<String, dynamic> draft) apply, {String? key, bool reseed = false})` — Applies [apply] to the draft as a keystroke, the autosave writing it in its turn; [key] is the key that changed, for the draft's observers, and [reseed] has the form's boxes read the draft again.
  - `Listenable get listenable` — Notifies whenever the draft changes, typed or applied.
- **class `DraftRefusal`** — What an open draft says about its last write: the error that left it unwritten, for an action [OpenDrafts.settleOrRefusal] stopped to say why in the save's own words.
  - `Object? get refusal` — The error of the write that left this draft unwritten, or null where it is clean, waiting or writing.
- **enum `DraftChangeKind`** — What happened to the open drafts: a form opened, went away, or moved to another file (§6.14).
  - values: `added`, `removed`, `moved`
- **class `DraftChange`** — One change of the open drafts, heard by the sync, which sends a document once its form is left (§6.14).
  - `const DraftChange(this.projectKey, this.kind)` — Names the film of the draft that changed and how.
  - `final String? projectKey` — The film the draft was built for; null only for unbound test seams.
  - `final DraftChangeKind kind` — Whether the draft was added, removed or moved to another file.
- **class `OpenDrafts`** — The drafts open across the app, and the writes no form waits for any more.
  - `static bool get idle` — Whether nothing is open and nothing is being written: no draft for [settleOpen] to write first.
  - `static void add(OpenDraft draft)`
  - `static void remove(OpenDraft draft)`
  - `static void moved(OpenDraft draft)` — Says that [draft] now edits another file: the file it left may be sent (§6.14).
  - `static Stream<DraftChange> get changes` — Every draft added, removed or moved to another file, heard after the change (§6.14).
  - `static Stream<void> get writesSettled` — An event each time the last tracked write ends, so that a send held for it can go (§6.14).
  - `static bool get writesPending` — Whether a draft's write is in flight: no document is read for sending meanwhile (§6.14).
  - `static bool openIn(String projectKey)` — Whether a form is open on a file of the film [projectKey].
  - `static OpenDraft? of(String stem, {String? projectKey})` — The draft open on the file [stem], if a form is.
  - `static void track(Future<void> write)` — A write in flight, waited for by [settleOpen] and by every pass of [settleUntilQuiet] until it completes: a draft's own as it starts, and one left behind by a form gone.
  - `static Future<bool> settleOpen()` — Settles every draft ([OpenDraft.settle]) and waits for every write left behind, for an action that reads files the way they are on disk — a fork copies one (§13.1).
  - `static Future<Object?> settleOrRefusal()` — Settles every draft as [settleOpen] does, and answers why one could not be written, or null where every one is clean afterwards.
  - `static const maxSettlePasses` — The most passes [settleUntilQuiet] makes: typing that outruns five writes in a row is still being typed, and what waits on it does not go on under it.
  - `static Future<Object?> settleUntilQuiet()` — Settles every draft as [settleOrRefusal] does, pass after pass while one leaves something to write — a form opened meanwhile, or one typed into after its own write — up to [maxSettlePasses] passes, so that nothing typ…
- **class `DraftsNotSettledException`** — An open draft could not be written, so an action that writes beside it — an add, a remove, a move — did nothing.
  - `const DraftsNotSettledException()`
- **class `DraftObserver`** — Hears every change a form's draft takes: the entity being edited, the key that changed, and the draft's value at that key after the change.
  - `void onChange(Entity entity, String? key, Object? value)` — [value] is a deep copy, so an observer never writes into a draft.
- **class `DraftObservers`** — The observers of every draft; empty in the product.
  - `static void add(DraftObserver observer)`
  - `static void remove(DraftObserver observer)`
  - `static void notify(Entity entity, String? key, [Object? value])` — Tells every observer, copying [value] once per observer, so that what one does with it cannot reach another or the draft.

### `lib/src/import_proposals.dart`

- **class `ImportOrigin`** — Where an import proposal came from: the plug-in, its function and, for the assistant, its operation (§6.18).
  - `const ImportOrigin({required this.plugin, required this.function, this.operationId})`
  - `final String plugin` — The plug-in's tag, as its door passes it: the review names the plug-in by it.
  - `final String function` — The function whose call proposed the import.
  - `final String? operationId` — The operation the proposal belongs to, which takes it away when it ends.
- **class `ImportProposal`** — One import waiting for the person: the document, the plan as they review it and the stages already written.
  - `ImportProposal({ required String id, required Map<String, Object?> document, Map<String, Object?>? base, required ImportOrigin origin, required Str…` — Freezes copies of the documents, JSON values only, so that no edit of a caller's maps changes what was reviewed.
  - `final String id` — The proposal's id, the one a door answered with.
  - `final Map<String, Object?> document` — The import document as proposed.
  - `final Map<String, Object?>? base` — The export the document was made against, where the plug-in named one.
  - `final ImportOrigin origin` — The plug-in call that proposed it.
  - `final String film` — The film's key (`projectKeyOf`) the proposal was made in.
  - `final Author? viewer` — The viewer the plan was made for, and the only one it is written as.
  - `final Guards guards` — Development mode's policy the plan was made under, and the only one it is written under.
  - `final DateTime proposedAt` — When the door held it.
  - `final ImportPlan plan` — The plan the person is shown; *Apply* writes only where a plan recomputed then is the same.
  - `final Map<ExchangeId, Map<ImportStage, String?>> stages` — The stages earlier applies completed, by change, with the stems they made: what *Apply again* resumes from.
  - `final bool deferred` — Whether the person put it aside with *Later*: the browser offers it again only when asked (§9.3).
  - `ImportProposal withReview(ImportPlan plan, {Map<ExchangeId, Map<ImportStage, String?>>? stages})` — The same proposal with another reviewed plan and the stages written so far.
  - `bool belongsTo(String? film, Author? viewer)` — Whether the proposal still belongs to the film open now, as the viewer of now.
- **class `ImportProposals`** — The import proposals waiting for the person, and the exports an operation keeps (§6.18, §7.1): a seam.
  - `static Listenable get changes` — Notified after every change of the proposals; not on a drop at read, which the reader already sees.
  - `static void add(ImportProposal proposal)` — Holds [proposal] for the person, after any held before it; one with the same id is replaced in its place.
  - `static void replace(ImportProposal proposal, {ImportProposal? expected})` — Replaces a held proposal with [proposal], keeping its place; one discarded meanwhile stays discarded, and where [expected] is given, one replaced meanwhile by another stays as it is.
  - `static void defer(ImportProposal shown)` — Puts [shown] aside with *Later*, after every other held proposal, so that the next one asked for is another; one let go or replaced since it was shown is not put aside, and a new document under its id is a new proposal.
  - `static void discard(String id)` — Lets the proposal [id] go, written or not.
  - `static List<ImportProposal> current({required String? film, required Author? viewer})` — The proposals of [film] for [viewer], in the order they came; every other one is dropped.
  - `static ImportProposal? of(String id, {required String? film, required Author? viewer})` — The proposal [id] where it belongs to [film] and [viewer]; dropped and null where it does not.
  - `static void retainExport(String operationId, String exportId, Map<String, Object?> document)` — Keeps an export [document] under [exportId] for the operation [operationId] until it is released.
  - `static Map<String, Object?>? exportOf(String operationId, String exportId)` — The export [exportId] the operation [operationId] kept, or null.
  - `static void release(String operationId)` — Ends what the operation [operationId] kept, when it is cancelled, fails or ends with nothing to propose: its exports and its proposals.
  - `static void clear()` — Forgets every proposal and every kept export.

### `lib/src/lending.dart`

- **function** `String usdOfCents(int cents)` — [cents] whole US cents as the list keeps a price ([SharedOffer.usd]): 2 → `'0.02'`, 20 → `'0.2'`, 100 → `'1'`.
- **function** `int? centsOfUsd(String usd)` — The whole cents of [usd] as [usdOfCents] writes it, or null for a text not of that shape.
- **class `SharedOffer`** — One offer this computer shares, as the person fixed it (§6.11, *Lending*): a plug-in's sharing operation on one server, one stack with the options the person chose on it, named and priced.
  - `const SharedOffer({ required this.id, required this.tag, required this.function, required this.model, this.server, required this.stack, this.params…` — An offer; [params] is kept as given.
  - `final String id` — The offer's id on the website: a UUID made once on this computer and kept for good.
  - `final String tag` — The plug-in's tag.
  - `final String function, model` — The sharing operation's `function` and `model`, as the plug-in's manifest declares them.
  - `final String stack` — The plug-in's way of running the model, as its options named it.
  - `final Map<String, Object?> params` — The options the person fixed on the stack, by the stack's own option names: `{resolution: '1024x1024'}`.
  - `final String name` — The person's name for it, made from the stack's label and the fixed options: *8 GB Quality · 1024x1024*.
  - `final String usd` — The price of one unit in US dollars, an exact decimal of whole cents with no trailing fractional zero: `'0.02'`, `'0.2'`; `'0'` is free.
  - `final bool enabled` — Whether the person has it on: only an enabled offer is published.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()` — The offer as the list keeps it.
  - `static SharedOffer? fromJson(Object? json)` — An offer as [toJson] wrote it, or null for an entry not of that shape — every build on a machine shares the preferences, so a value read may be anything.
  - `static List<SharedOffer> listOf(Object? json)` — The offers of a stored list: each entry of the shape, the rest left out; nothing where [json] is not a list.
- **class `LendingRefused`** — The website's refusal of a lending operation, by its code alone — or `unreachable` where nothing answered and `malformed` where the answer was not of the design's shape.
  - `const LendingRefused(this.code)` — A refusal under [code].
  - `final String code` — The error envelope's code, never its words.
- **class `LendingJobSummary`** — One job as the website summarises it, closed to what the supplier's loop and the requester read.
  - `const LendingJobSummary({ required this.id, required this.offerId, required this.state, this.priceCents, this.resultAvailable = false, this.closeRe…` — A job [id] of the offer [offerId], in [state] (`requested`, `accepted`, …).
  - `final String id`
  - `final String offerId`
  - `final String state`
  - `final int? priceCents` — The price frozen at preparation, in US cents.
  - `final bool resultAvailable` — Whether the result is published and still readable, whatever the money's state.
  - `final String? closeReason` — `refused`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `expired`, for a job closed without a result.
  - `final String? failCode` — The supplier's bounded code for a refusal or a failure.
  - `final int? retrieveUntil` — Until when the result's bytes may be read, in Unix milliseconds.
- **class `LendingJob`** — A job as a participant reads it: its summary, the frozen declaration, the input and, once published, the result.
  - `const LendingJob({required this.summary, this.declaration, this.input, this.result})` — A job of [summary], with the [declaration], [input] and [result] the website retains for it.
  - `final LendingJobSummary summary`
  - `final Map<String, Object?>? declaration`
  - `final Object? input` — The buyer's input as the website keeps it: any JSON, opaque to the website, for the supplier to judge.
  - `final Map<String, Object?>? result` — The supplier's result, a JSON object opaque to the website; its media travel inside it by URL.
- **class `LentOffer`** — One published offer this account may render on, as discovery lists it: the declaration's plug-in, its configuration and rates, and the website's derived facts.
  - `const LentOffer({ required this.offerId, required this.version, required this.pluginId, required this.pluginVersion, required this.configuration, r…` — The offer [offerId] at [version], declared for [pluginId] at [pluginVersion].
  - `final String offerId`
  - `final String version`
  - `final String pluginId`
  - `final String pluginVersion`
  - `final Map<String, Object?> configuration` — The declaration's public configuration: for a render, its `function`, `model` and `unit`.
  - `final bool own` — Offered by this same account.
  - `final bool free` — Free to this account — any of its persons named by the lender, or in a group the lender names — advisory until preparation.
  - `final bool available` — Its supplier is available now.
  - `final bool published` — This version is the offer's published one.
  - `final String? lender` — The lender's public username, its account's primary one; null where it has claimed none.
- **class `AudienceSettings`** — Who may use this account's published offers (`/v1/lending/settings`, §6.11, *Lending*): the website's revision of the setting, the persons and groups — by id — that use them free, and whether the public may buy them.
  - `const AudienceSettings({required this.revision, required this.freeWith, required this.publicPaid})` — The setting at [revision].
  - `final int revision` — The revision the website keeps; a write names the one it read, and a stale one is refused `terms-conflict`.
  - `final List<String> freeWith` — The ids of the persons and groups that use the offers free, each the design's `Uuid`.
  - `final bool publicPaid` — Whether anyone else may buy the offers at their price.
- **class `PublicName`** — A name as anybody may read it (`GET /v1/community/names/{username}`): its id, its username and its kind, `person` or `group` — exactly those, as the website answers them.
  - `const PublicName({required this.id, required this.username, required this.kind})` — The name [username], whose id is [id].
  - `final String id`
  - `final String username`
  - `final String kind`
- **class `Lending`** — The website's lending, the supplier's side and the requester's: each method one operation of the design, answering its value or throwing [LendingRefused].
  - `const Lending()` — Creates a client without account or transport work.
  - `static Lending get current` — The installed client; [NoLending] by default.
  - `static void install(Lending lending)` — Installs [lending] without calling it.
  - `static final published` — The ids of this computer's shared offers the website acknowledged as published, as the lending loop last heard it: set by the loop at each turn, emptied at sign-out and when the loop stops, and read by *Share my plugi…
  - `Future<String> declare(String offerId, Map<String, Object?> declaration)` — Declares the offer [offerId] with [declaration] (`PUT /v1/lending/offers/{offerId}`), answering the version the website hashed it to: the same for an equal declaration, another for a changed one.
  - `Future<void> publish(String offerId, String version, bool published)` — Publishes the offer [offerId] at [version], or withdraws it, as [published] says (`PUT /v1/lending/offers/{offerId}/publication`): a desired state, the last write winning.
  - `Future<void> setAvailability(String state)` — Sets this device's availability: `available`, `busy` or `unavailable` (`PUT /v1/lending/availability`).
  - `Future<List<LendingJobSummary>> inbox()` — The inbox's first page: this device's requested and accepted jobs, oldest first, fifty a page (`GET /v1/lending/jobs`, no query); reading it refreshes this device's presence.
  - `Future<List<LentOffer>> offers()` — The published offers this account may render on, discovery's first page (`GET /v1/lending/offers`).
  - `Future<List<LentOffer>> supplied()` — Every version of every offer this account owns, published or not, on any device, every page (`GET /v1/lending/offers?role=supplier`, the bearer alone).
  - `Future<LendingJob> prepare(String id, {required String offerId, required String version, required List<({String unit, String quantity})> quantities…` — Prepares the job [id] on the offer [offerId] at [version] — [quantities] per unit, the opaque JSON [input], at the [expectedPriceCents] the person was shown (`POST /v1/lending/jobs`).
  - `Future<LendingJob> job(String id)` — The job [id] (`GET /v1/lending/jobs/{id}`).
  - `Future<void> decide(String id, String decision, {String? code, Map<String, Object?>? result})` — `accept`, `refuse`, `fail`, `complete` or `cancel` on the job [id], with [code] for a refusal or a failure and the opaque [result] for `complete`, which publishes it (`POST …/decision`).
  - `Future<AudienceSettings> audience()` — This account's audience (`GET /v1/lending/settings`); refused `lending-unavailable` where no client is installed.
  - `Future<AudienceSettings> setAudience(AudienceSettings settings)` — Writes the audience as [settings], own devices fixed, naming the revision read (`PUT /v1/lending/settings`), and answers what the website keeps now; a stale revision is `terms-conflict`.
- **class `NoLending`** — The client of a build that installed none: every operation is refused `lending-unavailable`, and nothing is sent.
  - `const NoLending()` — The inert client.

  - `final ConversationOperationCode code` — What the operation achieved or why it could not run.
  - `final ProviderUnavailableReason? reason` — The route's typed unavailable reason, where applicable.
- **enum `ConversationFinishReason`** — Why a finish returned its frozen transcript.
  - values: `finished`, `timedOut`, `ended`, `closed`, `unsupported`
- **class `ConversationFinished`** — A finish outcome that preserves an explicitly complete or partial frozen transcript.
  - `const ConversationFinished({required this.transcript, required this.reason})` — Captures the retained transcript and the terminal drain outcome.
  - `final ConversationTranscript transcript` — The transcript frozen before any separate finalizer is invoked.
  - `final ConversationFinishReason reason` — Whether drain completed, timed out, was interrupted or was unsupported.
- **class `ConversationSession`** — A bound native conversation whose resource ownership begins only on explicit Start.
  - `const ConversationSession()` — Creates a session interface without connecting a transport.
  - `ConversationBinding get binding` — The immutable choice captured by open, retained through Finish and teardown.
  - `ConversationSnapshot get snapshot` — The current state and transcript without a request or capture side effect.
  - `Stream<void> get changes` — Signals after the visible session snapshot changes.
  - `Stream<ConversationCaption> get captions` — Admitted caption revisions keyed by turn, still delivered during the finish drain.
  - `Stream<ConversationUsage> get usage` — Provider-reported units, still delivered during drain without inferring billing.
  - `Future<ConversationOperationResult> start()` — Admits only a ready, funded session after explicit action, acquiring native resources then.
  - `Future<ConversationOperationResult> mute(bool muted)` — Changes capture muting without retargeting the frozen session binding.
  - `Future<ConversationOperationResult> interrupt()` — Interrupts spoken output through the bound native provider protocol.
  - `Future<ConversationOperationResult> end()` — Immediately tears down all resources and retains the transcript without finalizing or writing.
  - `Future<ConversationFinished> finish()` — Stops capture, commits pending audio and stops spoken output before draining admitted caption events.
  - `Future<ConversationOperationResult> close()` — Immediately tears down resources, including while Finish drains, and retains the visible transcript.
- **class `NativeConversation`** — The host-installed native conversation door, unsupported until an implementation is installed.
  - `const NativeConversation()` — Creates a service without accessing audio, credentials or sockets.
  - `static NativeConversation get current` — The installed native service, unsupported by default.
  - `static void install(NativeConversation service)` — Installs an implementation without opening or starting a session.
  - `static Stream<void> get installations` — Signals replacement to consumers that already read support.
  - `ConversationSupport get support` — The implemented capability's truthful support state.
  - `Stream<void> get changes` — Signals after support changes, without admitting a conversation.
  - `ConversationSession open(ConversationBinding binding)` — Captures the frozen choice only, acquiring no microphone and connecting no socket.
- **class `NoNativeConversation`** — The inert native service, answering unsupported without throwing a sentence.
  - `const NoNativeConversation()` — Creates the unavailable service.
- **class `UnavailableConversationSession`** — An inert bound session retaining an unavailable empty transcript and opening nothing.
  - `UnavailableConversationSession(this.binding)` — Captures the chosen binding without native work.

### `lib/src/page_access.dart`

- **enum `GuardNotice`** — A red line a page shows in development mode.
  - values: `otherAuthor`, `notDirector`, `libraryFile`, `noHandle`, `sessionCopy`, `readOnlyFolder`, `libraryReadOnly`
- **enum `ChildrenLock`** — Why a version's `children` may not be changed.
  - values: `noHandle`, `readOnly`, `notYours`
- **class `PageAccess`**
  - `const PageAccess({ required this.editable, required this.canSetOfficial, required this.canPick, required this.choosesNothing, required this.canLabe…`
  - `factory PageAccess.of(FilmProject project, Entity entity, Author? viewer, Guards guards)`
  - `final bool editable` — The form writes: the viewer's own version, or — in development mode — anybody's, the shared library's included where the library can be written.
  - `final bool canSetOfficial` — The star can be pressed: never on a discarded version, which a pointer would name as none (§6.1).
  - `final bool canPick` — The check can choose the version in use: never on a plug-in (§6.11), nor on a discarded version (§6.1).
  - `final bool choosesNothing` — Neither the check nor the star chooses anything here: a plug-in, whose installed version runs whatever the film (§6.11).
  - `final bool canLabel` — The version label can be edited.
  - `final bool canRunPlugins` — *Plugins…* may run a plug-in on the file shown: from anybody's version, since the run never writes over it.
  - `final List<GuardNotice> notices` — The red lines the page shows, in this order.
  - `final ChildrenLock? childrenLock` — Why this version's `children` may not be changed.
  - `bool get canEditChildren` — Whether a folder or scene may be added to, removed from or moved in this version's `children`.
  - `static bool canCreateVersions(FilmProject project, Author? viewer)` — Whether the viewer may make new versions in [project] (§8.2).

### `lib/src/plugin_readiness.dart`

- **function** `String? pluginWords(Object? value, {int most = 300})` — **A plug-in's own words, cleaned for a card or a page** (§6.11): at most [most] characters, or null for none.
- **enum `PluginSwitchNotSaved`** — Which switch of the person's could not be saved.
  - values: `off`, `on`

- **class `PluginStatusDetails`** — The measured facts of a plug-in's status that the app shows with its own labels and units (the definition's `Status.details`); each one absent is unknown, never zero.

  - `factory PluginStatusDetails.fromJson(Object? details)` — The four facts copied out of a status's `details`, and nothing else of the plug-in's own.

  - `final String? gpu` — The graphics card the service runs on, as the service names it.
  - `final int? gpuMemoryBytes` — That card's memory, in bytes.
  - `final int? memoryBytes` — The memory of the computer the service runs on, in bytes.
  - `bool get isEmpty` — Whether the plug-in gave none of the four, so that nothing is drawn for them.
- **class `PluginStatusFact`** — What a plug-in last said of whether it can work: one of the four states, its own words and the facts it measured.
  - `const PluginStatusFact(this.state, {this.message, this.details = const PluginStatusDetails()})` — A state, with the plug-in's words and facts where it gave them.
  - `final PluginStatusState state` — Which of the four states it said: ready, unconfigured, unavailable or degraded.
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own words, in the language they were asked in; null where it gave none, or where the app's language changed since, so that one line is never in two languages.
  - `final PluginStatusDetails details` — What it measured, of the four facts the app shows; each one it did not give unknown.
  - `PluginStatusFact withoutMessage()` — This fact without the plug-in's words, for a language other than the one it was asked in.
- **enum `PluginLifecycleProblemKind`** — What became of the last operation of a plug-in's lifecycle, or of its last *Check*, where it did not succeed.
  - values: `activationFailed`, `activationTimedOut`, `activationHung`, `notPublished`, `checkFailed`, `cleanupFailed`, `cleanupTimedOut`, `cleanupSkipped`
- **class `PluginLifecycleProblem`** — Why the last operation of a plug-in's lifecycle, or its last *Check*, did not succeed: its kind, a code that is safe to show and to log, and the plug-in's own words where it gave some.
  - `const PluginLifecycleProblem(this.kind, {this.code, this.reason, this.path, this.message})` — A problem of [kind], with what is known of it.
  - `final PluginLifecycleProblemKind kind` — What did not succeed, and so which sentence says it.
  - `final String? code` — The call's failure code (`failed`, `limit`, `refused`, `badResult`, …), or the plug-in's own problem code where it is a token; never prose.
  - `final String? reason` — The code's reason, where it has one (`wall`, `no-server`).
  - `final String? path` — Where an answer failed the definition (`status.state`), for `badResult`.
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own words, in the language they were asked in; null after the app's language changed.
  - `bool get retryable` — Whether *Try again* is offered: for an activation or a check that did not succeed of a plug-in still on — never for a clean-up, nor for one that hung or did not come on, which is off and which its switch, or *Allow*,…
  - `bool get isCleanup` — Whether it is about the plug-in being turned off.
  - `PluginLifecycleProblem withoutMessage()` — This problem without the plug-in's words, for a language other than the one they were in.
- **class `PluginReadiness`** — What the app knows now of whether a plug-in can work, the one record its card and its page both draw (§6.11).
  - `const PluginReadiness({ required this.stem, this.phase = PluginLifecyclePhase.idle, this.declaresLifecycle = false, this.fact, this.saysNothing = f…` — What is known of [stem].
  - `final String stem` — The plug-in this is known of.
  - `final PluginLifecyclePhase phase` — Where its own work stands: idle, being turned on or off, or checked.
  - `final bool declaresLifecycle` — Whether its manifest declares the `lifecycle` interface, so that turning it on or off asks its code.
  - `final PluginStatusFact? fact` — What it last said; null where nothing is known — the app started since, it was turned on with nothing to ask, or what it said no longer holds because its code, its grants, its settings or its keys changed.
  - `final bool saysNothing` — It was asked, and its code has no `status`: *Check* says so, and its other functions still run.
  - `final PluginLifecycleProblem? problem` — Why the last operation did not succeed; null where it did, or nothing ran.
  - `final PluginSwitchNotSaved? switchNotSaved` — The person's switch that could not be saved, where one was not: an Off, off for this session and perhaps on again at the next start; or an On, which did not come on.
  - `bool get isBusy` — Whether a phase is under way.

- **class `PluginDevFunction`** — One function the developer page offers to call.
  - `const PluginDevFunction({required this.name, required this.label, required this.kind, this.example})`
  - `final String name` — The function of the plug-in's object.
  - `final String label` — What to show in the pull-down: its words where it has any, else its name.
  - `final String kind` — `action`, `hook`, `offer` — or `other`, the name a person typed.
  - `final Object? example` — The arguments to fill the box with.
- **class `PluginDevRun`** — One run made from the developer page.
  - `const PluginDevRun({ required this.outcome, required this.elapsed, required this.lines, required this.lastRunPath, this.mode = PluginDevMode.app, t…`
  - `final PluginCallOutcome outcome`
  - `final Duration elapsed`
  - `final PluginDevMode mode` — How it was called, and what the function was called with.
  - `final Object? request`
  - `final List<PluginDevLine> lines` — Every `ctx.log` line of the call and a row per door it used, in order.
  - `final String lastRunPath` — Where this run was written, for a person to open and an agent to read.
- **class `PluginDevLine`** — One line of the developer page's log: a `ctx.log` the code made, or a door it used.
  - `const PluginDevLine({ required this.at, required this.kind, required this.message, this.data, this.detail, this.milliseconds, this.by, })`
  - `final int at` — Milliseconds since the run began, so a reader sees what took the time.
  - `final String kind` — The line holds what crossed into JavaScript: `log` for a line the code wrote, else the door's own name (`http`, `call`, `storage.get`, `project.script`, …).
  - `final String message` — What the code said, or what the door was asked for.
  - `final String? data` — The JSON the code passed, or the door's answer, cut at 64 KB with a mark.
  - `final String? detail` — A door's own summary: a status, a size, a refusal's reason.
  - `final String? by` — The tag of the plug-in that made this line, where it is **not** the one the page ran.
  - `final int? milliseconds` — How long a door took, where it waited.
- **class `PluginOffer`** — One function a plug-in offers, in its own words.
  - `const PluginOffer({required this.name, required this.label, this.help, this.example})`
  - `final String name`
  - `final String label` — The offering plug-in's words for it, in the app's language.
  - `final String? help`
  - `final Object? example` — A value of the arguments it takes, for a reader and for the developer page's argument box.
- **class `PluginCalls`** — The calls one plug-in declares on another, as consent lists them.
  - `const PluginCalls({required this.tag, required this.name, required this.labels, this.installed = true, this.keyPlatforms = const []})`
  - `final String tag`
  - `final String name` — The called plug-in's name, or its tag where it is not installed.
  - `final List<String> labels` — What each called function does, in the words of the plug-in that owns it.
  - `final bool installed` — False where the plug-in called is not installed: the page then says so, and every call answers `noProvider`.
  - `final List<String> keyPlatforms` — The platforms, by their names, of the keys the called plug-in **owns**.
- **class `PluginServer`** — A `server` setting as consent names it.
  - `const PluginServer({required this.key, required this.label, this.defaultAddress})`
  - `final String key`
  - `final String label` — The setting's words in the app's language.
  - `final String? defaultAddress` — The address it starts with, which can only ever be this computer.
- **class `PluginKeySlot`** — One card of Provider keys.
  - `const PluginKeySlot({required this.keyId, required this.slot, required this.platform, this.label, this.help, this.auth = 'key', this.account, this.…`
  - `final String keyId` — `<owner>:<slot>`.
  - `final String slot`
  - `final String platform`
  - `final String? label`
  - `final String? help`
  - `final String? planLabel` — The owning platform OAuth block's plan name, independent of the slot label.
  - `final String auth` — The manifest's authentication kind, independent of the platform's copied key.
  - `final String? account` — The signed-in label from this slot's existing key record; never a credential read.
  - `final DateTime? expiresAt` — The signed-in credential expiry from the same key record.
  - `String get storeName` — The credential store's name for it.
  - `String get preferenceName` — The preference that holds its state.
- **class `PluginKeyOwner`** — A section of Provider keys: an owner and its slots.
  - `const PluginKeyOwner({required this.owner, required this.name, required this.slots, this.platforms = const {}})`
  - `final String owner` — The plug-in's tag.
  - `final String name`
  - `final List<PluginKeySlot> slots`
  - `final Map<String, PlatformFile> platforms` — The owner's own platform files, by id, for its slots on a platform the catalogue does not define (§14.9): a key's file is the catalogue's or its owner's, never another plug-in's.
- **class `PluginInterface`** — One interface a plug-in implements (`implements`, §14.4), as a page lists it.
  - `const PluginInterface({ required this.name, this.platform, this.platformName, this.models = const [], this.kinds = const [], this.takes = const [],…`
  - `final String name` — `render`, `text`, `platform`, `transform`, …
  - `final String? platform` — The platform's id, where the interface asks for one.
  - `final String? platformName` — The platform file's name for it (*fal*), where one is known.
  - `final List<String> models` — The catalogue entries it speaks for; empty is *any on that platform*.
  - `final List<String> kinds` — What it describes, for `reference-analysis`: `image`, `audio` or both; empty for any other interface.
  - `final List<String> takes` — The file extensions of the media it takes, for `reference-analysis`, lowercase; empty where it names none, and then it takes any media of its kinds.
  - `final Map<String, Object?> declared` — The manifest's declaration of the interface, as written (`catalog`, `target`, `platform`, …).
- **class `PluginProvider`** — A plug-in that provides a hook, and for which platform.
  - `const PluginProvider({required this.tag, required this.name, required this.hook, this.platform, this.platformName, this.preferred = false})`
  - `final String tag`
  - `final String name`
  - `final String hook`
  - `final String? platform`
  - `final String? platformName` — The platform file's name for [platform] (*OpenRouter*), where one is known.
  - `final bool preferred`
- **class `PluginCallControl`** — Progress and cancellation of a running call, shared by the page that started it.
  - `final progress`
  - `final partial` — The running streamed call's visible text, appended in order by the host and cleared only by the control's owner.
  - `final note` — The running call's one current note — a passing word of what the model is doing, set by `ctx.note` (§6.11a) — replaced by the next, empty when there is none; never part of [partial] or of any message.
  - `int call` — The model call of the turn under way, numbered from 1 by the assistant's host; 0 outside a turn's call.
  - `ValueListenable<bool> get cancelled`
  - `void cancel()`
- **class `PluginCallOutcome`** — What a call came to.
  - `const PluginCallOutcome()`
  - `PluginCallOutcomeWords get words` — What `labels.dart`'s `pluginOutcomeText` reads of this outcome.
- **class `PluginCallDone`** — A call's value, and what it wrote: new versions' stems, takes' names.
  - `const PluginCallDone({this.value, this.message, this.messageText, this.written = const []})`
  - `final Object? value`
  - `final String? message` — An action's message key and the text it came to in the app's language.
  - `final String? messageText`
  - `final List<String> written`
- **class `PluginCallFailed`** — Why a call has no value: `failed` (with the plug-in's own [message]), `limit` ([reason]: time, memory, stack, result, wall), `cancelled`, `hung`, `refused` ([reason]), `disabled`, `noProvider`, `notAvailable`, `stale`.
  - `const PluginCallFailed(this.code, {this.reason, this.message, this.file, this.line, this.column, this.path, this.stage})`
  - `final String code`
  - `final String? reason`
  - `final String? message`
  - `final String? stage` — Where a request door's refusal came: `admission`, before anything left the machine, or `transport`; null for any other failure.
  - `final String? path` — Where an answer failed the contract, in the answer's own terms — `outputs[0].mime` — for the code `badResult`.
  - `final String? file` — The plug-in's own code file the failure came from, and the place in it.
  - `final int? line`
  - `final int? column`
  - `String? get at` — `file:line:column`, or null where there is no position: what a page and the developer page show after the message.
- **enum `PluginStatusState`** — The four states a plug-in's `status` may answer (§14.4): whether it can do its work now, in words a person can act on.
  - values: `ready`, `unconfigured`, `unavailable`, `degraded`
  - `static PluginStatusState? byName(String name)`
- **class `PluginCheckResult`** — What a *Check* came to.
  - `const PluginCheckResult()`
- **class `PluginChecked`** — What the plug-in said about itself: a state, its own words where it gave any, and the facts it measured.
  - `const PluginChecked(this.state, {this.message, this.details = const PluginStatusDetails()})`
  - `final PluginStatusState state`
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own message, in the person's language, where it gave one.
  - `final PluginStatusDetails details` — The facts of its `details` the app shows, copied; each absent one is unknown.
- **class `PluginSaysNothing`** — **The plug-in's code has no `status`**, which api 1 asks of every plug-in.
  - `const PluginSaysNothing()`
- **class `PluginCheckFailed`** — The check did not finish: the call's own outcome.
  - `const PluginCheckFailed(this.failure)`
  - `final PluginCallFailed failure`
- **class `PluginKeyCheck`** — A plug-in's answer about a candidate key.
  - `const PluginKeyCheck({required this.accepted, this.message, this.code})`
  - `final bool accepted`
  - `final String? message` — The plug-in's own words, shown under the key's boxes.
  - `final String? code` — Where the check itself failed: the call's code.
- **class `PluginInstallOutcome`** — What installing a zip came to.
  - `const PluginInstallOutcome({this.stem, this.refused, this.field})`
  - `final String? stem` — The installed plug-in, which then asks for consent.
  - `final String? refused` — A problem's code when the zip was refused, `writeFailed` or `failed` when installing it failed, or `reloadFailed` when its files were written and the plug-ins could not be read again.
  - `final String? field`
- **class `NoPluginRuntime`** — The runtime of a build that installs none: no plug-in exists.
  - `const NoPluginRuntime()`

### `lib/src/project_provider.dart`

- **variable** `const AssetProjectSource bundledLibrary` — The bundled seed of the shared library, read in place where the app has no files of its own (the web).
- **variable** `final libraryProvider` — The shared library of models, platforms and plugins (§14.5).
- **variable** `final projectProvider` — The opened project.
- **class `ProjectImportException`** — A failed FDX import, with a localizable code and no screenplay or filesystem error text.
  - `const ProjectImportException(this.code)` — Creates the refusal presented inside the import dialog.
  - `final String code` — The diagnostic code, such as invalid_xml, read_failed, write_failed or drafts_unsaved.
- **variable** `final projectClosedProvider` — Whether the person closed the project: the page then shows no project until one is opened or created.
- **class `ProjectClosedController`**
  - `void set(bool closed)`
- **variable** `final projectSourceKeyProvider` — Identifies *which* source is open, as opposed to its current contents.
- **class `CreatedProject`** — What *New project* made: the project file, which the app opens on *Edit* (§9.2), and the scene the script starts with.
  - `const CreatedProject({required this.project, required this.scene})`
  - `final VersionStem project`
  - `final VersionStem scene`
- **class `OpenRefusedException`** — Another film was not opened, made or copied to because an open draft of this one could not be written first (§7).
  - `const OpenRefusedException(this.refusal)`
  - `final Object refusal` — Why the draft was not written.
- **variable** `const Duration kSettleBeforeLeaving` — How long the drafts may take to be written before another film opens: as long as closing the window gives them (the app's `DraftsBeforeExit.limit`), past which the open is refused.
- **class `NoLongerWantedException`** — A write whose caller no longer wanted it when its queue reached it (§7.4): nothing was written.
  - `const NoLongerWantedException()` — A refusal of a write its caller's check declined in the queue.
- **class `ViewerChangedException`** — A write asked as one viewer that reached its queue under another (§7.4): nothing was written.
  - `const ViewerChangedException(this.viewer, this.current)` — A refusal of a write asked as [viewer] while the username is now [current].
  - `final Author viewer` — The author the write was asked as.
  - `final Author? current` — The viewer when the write's turn came; null where there is none.
- **class `ProjectNotOpenedException`** — A project whose files were written whole but whose folder could not be read back — it would not list, or not load — so it was not opened, and the project on screen stays (§9.2).
  - `const ProjectNotOpenedException(this.path, this.cause)`
  - `final String path` — The folder the project was written in, or the session's label where it has none.
  - `final Object cause` — What the read answered.
- **variable** `final folderSourceProvider` — How a folder on disk is read as a project: the store's `directoryProjectSource`, and a test's stand-in for a folder that writes and will not list.
- **variable** `final folderWatchProvider` — How the open film's folder is watched for documents changed outside the app (§6.1b): the platform's `watchFolder`, and a test's watch over streams of its own.
- **class `IndexNotPublishedException`** — A write landed, but the index could not be published after it — the folder would not list — so the view is behind the folder until it is read again (§7.5).
  - `const IndexNotPublishedException(this.cause, {this.answer})` — The publication's failure, [cause], after a gesture whose body answered [answer].
  - `final Object cause` — What the listing answered.
  - `final Object? answer` — What the gesture's writes answered before its publication failed — the stem written, say — so that its caller says what landed; null where the body answered nothing.
- **class `ProjectController`**
  - `WriteRecord get record` — The write record, for a writer made outside the controller — an insertion job's — so that its writes are in [view] as they land and in the next publication unread (§7.5).
  - `Future<void> Function()? beforePublish` — Runs once, as a gesture is about to publish its index, and is spent before it runs: the seam where a test types or edits a file between a gesture's writes and its publication.
  - `FilmProject? get baseIndex` — [_base], read-only, so a test can see that an overtaken re-read left it alone.
  - `FilmProject? get view` — The film as every decision reads it (§7.5): the published index with the record's landed writes of this film and its library laid over it, built without a read; the published index itself while nothing has landed since.
  - `FilmProject? get baseView` — [baseIndex] with the record's landed writes laid over it, before any viewer's pick is applied: what another viewer's film is resolved from, as [view] is the viewer's (§7.5).
  - `Future<String> copySessionTo(String parentPath)` — Copies every file of the open session, including media, into a new folder and opens it there (§4.1).
  - `Future<void> openSample()` — Opens the sample afresh: a new extraction, made once the film being left has settled, so that an open refused replaces nothing and makes no folder.
  - `Future<void> close()` — *Close project*: every open draft is written first, and the film's documents are sent within what remains of [kSettleBeforeLeaving] (§6.14), then the page shows no project.
  - `Future<void> openDirectory(String path)` — Opens a folder on disk.
  - `Future<VersionStem> importScript({ required String path, required String parentPath, required String epochLabel, })` — Imports a screenplay file into a fresh folder, then opens its complete index without replacing the old film on failure.
  - `Future<CreatedProject> createProject({ required String parentPath, required String tag, required Author author, String? name, required String epoch…` — Creates a project — `<parentPath>/<tag>/` on disk where folders can be made, else a session-only project in memory — writes its manifest (§4.4) and the creator's first `pj` version (§8), and opens it once it has been…
  - `Future<bool> refresh({bool library = false, String reason = 'asked'})` — Reads the current source again whole, picking up files changed on disk: a publication of kind `reread` (§7.5).
  - `Future<bool> noticeWritten({Map<String, String?> written = const {}, String gesture = 'noticed', bool publish = true})` — Takes files written by something that is no recorded writer into the record, then publishes unless told not to.
  - `Future<void> selectProject(String stem)` — Answers the project chooser (§4.1) with one of the candidates.
  - `({String choice, bool landed})? inUseRecorded(Entity entity, {Author? viewer})` — The recorded choice, in flight or landed and unpublished, that makes [entity] the version in use, or null.
  - `Future<T> publishingOnce<T>(String name, Future<T> Function() body)` — Runs [body], every gesture landing its writes meanwhile without publishing them, then publishes the film once (§7.5).
  - `Future<void> updateManifest(Map<String, Object?> Function(Map<String, Object?> json) change)` — Changes the manifest with the current viewer and guards, one gesture.
  - `Future<Entity?> saveEntity(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json, {String? projectKey})` — Saves the viewer's own version with new content, one gesture.
  - `Future<Entity?> saveEntityAs(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json, {String? projectKey, Author? as})` — [saveEntity], written as [as] where given, which must be the viewer ([writingAs]).
  - `Future<VersionStem> createEntity({ required EntityType type, required String tag, String? epoch, required String name, String? kind, })` — A new character or location as the viewer's v1 at [epoch] (`ProjectWriter.createEntity`), one gesture.
  - `Future<VersionStem> createEntityAs({ required EntityType type, required String tag, String? epoch, required String name, String? kind, Author? as,…` — [createEntity], created as [as] where given, which must be the viewer ([writingAs]); with [draftLabel], the assistant's draft, labelled and not picked (`ProjectWriter.createEntity`).
  - `Future<VersionStem> fork(Entity entity, {Map<String, dynamic>? content, String? film, Author? as, String? draftLabel, Future<void> Function()? gate})` — Forks [entity] for the viewer (§13.1), one gesture, and returns the new stem so the caller can show it.
  - `Future<void> pinPick(Entity entity, {String? film, Future<void> Function()? gate})` — Pins [entity] as the viewer's own explicit pick, in their commentary file's queue, never following official as [setPick] does: the version in use made a choice before a second handle's version could make it ask (§4.1).
  - `Author? writingAs(Author? as)` — The author a write goes out as: the viewer, never another handle — the assistant writes as the person (§7.3).
  - `Future<({String epoch, VersionStem? project, bool relabelled, String reason})> declareEpoch(String label, {int? year, required String film, require…` — Declares an epoch labelled [label] on the project version in use, one gesture (§8.2).
  - `Future<VersionStem> createAtEpoch(EntityGroup group, String target, {required String sourceEpoch, required String boundSourceStem, required String…` — Makes the viewer's v1 of a character or location at a missing declared epoch, one gesture (§8.2).
  - `Future<List<Map<String,Object?>>> createCastVersions(Entity scene, {required String film, required Author? viewer, String? draftLabel})` — Creates missing cast character versions for a written scene without settling drafts or throwing (§7.3).
  - `Future<VersionStem> createOutfit(String character, String epoch, String name, {required String film, required Author viewer, String? draftLabel, Fu…` — Creates the viewer's outfit named [name] for [character] at [epoch], one gesture (Project Specification §9.2).
  - `Future<bool> setOfficial(Entity entity, {required bool official})` — Makes [entity] official (§13.2), or clears the pointer when [official] is false.
  - `Future<bool> setPick(Entity entity, {Author? viewer, bool unlessExplicitInUse = false, String? Function(Entity now)? unusable})` — Makes [entity] the viewer's pick (§13.4): the version used from now on.
  - `Future<bool> pickFromCheck(Entity entity)` — The check on the version row (§13.4): [entity] becomes the viewer's choice, even where it is already in use.
  - `Future<bool> abandonPick(Entity entity)` — Abandons the viewer's pick at [entity]'s epoch: it is removed, and the viewer is back on official (§13.4).
  - `Future<bool> keepPick(Entity entity)` — Keeps the viewer's pick, re-dating it so that its stale warning clears (§13.2).
  - `Future<({bool wrote, bool pickFollowed, bool parentFollowed})> setDiscarded(Entity entity, {Author? viewer, bool Function(FilmProject project)? sti…` — Sets the viewer's own [entity] aside: the one door for discarding (Project Specification §7, §6.1, §8.5).
  - `bool isCurrent(String film)` — Whether [film] is the film open now: not closed, not replaced, and not being left — another source asked, or opening.
  - `Future<bool> visit(Entity entity)` — Records that the viewer has [entity]'s media on screen (§13.4): the one door a page's visit goes through.
  - `Future<bool> deleteTake(String reference)` — Deletes the file of the viewer's own take [reference] names, and its thumbnail, one gesture (§9.0).
- **class `EpochBindingChangedException`** — What an epoch's write was bound to changed while it waited, so nothing was written (§8.2).
  - `const EpochBindingChangedException({this.reason = 'viewerChanged'})` — Refuses an epoch's write whose binding changed, for [reason]: the viewer's, unless another is said.
  - `final String reason` — What changed, as a code: `viewerChanged`, `projectNotBound`, `projectChanged`, `sourceChanged`, `targetUndeclared`, `targetExists` or `targetExistsDiscarded`.

### `lib/src/provider_funding.dart`

- **enum `ProviderUnavailableReason`** — A typed refusal that a consumer may later translate into a localized sentence.
  - values: `notConfigured`, `needsKey`, `needsSignIn`, `needsCredit`, `keyInvalid`, `keyDenied`, `checking`, `unknown`, `unsupportedRoute`, `dependencyDisabled`, `transportUnavailable`
- **variable** `const kPluginHttpOperation` — The operation word for a plug-in's HTTP call, as [ProviderFunding.funding] is asked about it.
- **variable** `const kConversationOperation` — The operation word for a voice conversation on credit (§6.6).
- **variable** `const kTranscriptionOperation` — The operation word for dictation's transcription on credit (§6.6).
- **variable** `const kPortalRefusalCodes` — The website's codes for a refused portal credential, on a `401`: the credential is let go ([ProviderFunding.portalRefused]) and nothing is sent again.
- **class `FundingBinding`** — A nonsecret opaque funding handle that a job retains by identity.
  - `FundingBinding({required this.providerTag, required this.operation})` — Captures only provider and operation, leaving credentials behind the implementation.
  - `final String providerTag` — The provider whose funding route was resolved.
  - `final String operation` — The operation the binding authorizes, rather than arbitrary provider work.
- **class `FundingResult`** — The resolved own-key, managed-credit or unavailable funding route.
  - `const FundingResult()` — Creates a typed funding result without admitting work or placing a hold.
- **class `OwnKeyFunding`** — A verified own-key route whose opaque binding a submitted job freezes.
  - `const OwnKeyFunding(this.binding)` — Captures a nonsecret binding for this result.
  - `final FundingBinding binding` — The implementation-owned binding retained unchanged through collection.
- **class `CreditFunding`** — An explicitly supported managed-credit route with an opaque frozen binding.
  - `const CreditFunding(this.binding)` — Captures a managed route, never inferring support from balance alone.
  - `final FundingBinding binding` — The implemented route's binding retained unchanged through collection.
- **class `FundingUnavailable`** — An unavailable route, with an explicit refusal rather than an inferred fallback.
  - `const FundingUnavailable(this.reason)` — Captures why funding is unavailable.
  - `final ProviderUnavailableReason reason` — The refusal a consumer translates when it shows the route.
- **typedef** `typedef PortalAccess` — Credit admission headers or the cause and code that prevented admission.
- **class `ProviderFunding`** — The host-owned funding resolver, whose queries never place holds or submit work.
  - `const ProviderFunding()` — Creates a resolver without credential, account or transport work.
  - `static ProviderFunding get current` — The installed resolver, not configured by default.
  - `static void install(ProviderFunding resolver)` — Installs a resolver without querying or activating it.
  - `static Stream<void> get installations` — Signals replacement to observers that already read the default.
  - `int get generation` — The revision advanced when credential, account or configuration bindings change.
  - `Stream<void> get changes` — Signals after the resolver generation changes.
  - `Future<FundingResult> funding(String providerTag, String operation)` — Resolves a nonsecret route without a hold, paid admission or silent invalid-key fallback.
  - `Future<Map<String, String>?> portalHeaders(String platform, String operation, String operationId)` — The headers a request on credit carries — the bearer and the portal credential for [operation]'s scope — or null where there is no credit (§6.6).
  - `Future<PortalAccess> portalAccess(String platform, String operation, String operationId, {Future<void>? abort})` — Acquires credit admission with cancellation and its refusal cause.
  - `Future<FundedReceipt?> receiptCancellable(String platform, String operation, String operationId, {Future<void>? abort})` — Reads a receipt with cancellation where the implementation supports it.
  - `Future<void> endCancellable(String platform, String operation, String operationId, {Future<void>? abort})` — Ends an operation with cancellation where the implementation supports it.
  - `void portalRefused(String platform, String operation, String operationId)` — The website refused the portal credential of [operation]'s scope (a 401): it is let go, so the next gesture asks anew; nothing is sent again.
  - `Future<FundedReceipt?> receipt(String platform, String operation, String operationId)` — The operation's receipt, `GET /v1/portal/operations/{id}`; null where it has not settled or could not be read.
  - `Future<void> end(String platform, String operation, String operationId)` — `POST /v1/portal/operations/{id}/end`, once; its outcome is logged and nothing waits on it.
  - `void balanceMoved(String reason)` — Credit may have moved — a call on credit closed, or an end was answered — so the balance is read again; [reason] names the trigger in the log (§6.6).
  - `void balanceMovedCancellable(String reason, {Future<void>? abort})` — Refreshes credit after a call, stopping that read with the turn's network work.
- **typedef** `typedef FundedReceipt` — What a funded operation's receipt says was charged and released, in whole US cents, and its id on the portal.
- **class `NoProviderFunding`** — The inert resolver, which has no configured or credit-backed route.
  - `const NoProviderFunding()` — Creates a resolver that never consults a credential or service.
- **class `FundingResolverSnapshot`** — An observed resolver and its revision, without performing a funding query.
  - `const FundingResolverSnapshot(this.resolver, this.generation)` — Captures the installed resolver and the generation observed with it.
  - `final ProviderFunding resolver` — The host-owned door a user action may query outside build.
  - `final int generation` — The revision under which the resolver was observed.

### `lib/src/queue_runner.dart`

- **variable** `final queueRunnerProvider` — Runs the queue's passes; the default answers *not available*, the app's composition runs the render queue.
- **function** `bool isQueueComplete(SetRecord record)` — A queue is complete only with at least one item and a take or error on every item (§6.15).
- **class `QueueRunner`** — The queue page's doors to a pass and to its items' jobs (§6.15).
  - `Future<String?> submit(BatchStem stem, {Set<int>? only})` — Runs one pass over the queue [stem]: null where it went through its items, else the code of why not.
  - `Future<QueuePreparation> prepare(InsertionTarget target)` — Prepares the saved words at [target] without writing or submitting anything.
  - `Future<QueuePreparation> prepareBeforeWriting(InsertionTarget target)` — Whether a prompt is worth writing for [target], before anything is paid (§9.3).
  - `Future<bool> finishInterrupted(BatchStem stem)` — Ends a pass that ended without its end, submitting nothing; false, with nothing written, where it may not.
  - `Future<bool> markNotSubmitted(BatchStem stem, int n)` — *Mark as not submitted* on the unresolved item [n]; false, with nothing written, where it may not.
  - `bool isLive(BatchStem stem)` — Whether a pass of [stem] is under way in this app.
  - `QueueJob? job(String id)` — The live job [id], else its terminal view heard this session without actions, else null.
  - `Future<String?> act(String id, String action)` — Sends [action] — one of [QueueJob.actions] — to job [id]: null where it was accepted, else the refusal's code.
  - `Stream<void> get changes` — Told when a pass starts or ends, or any job changes.
  - `Stream<QueueChainFailure> get chainFailures` — Failed terminal outcome writes, heard by the page while it is open.
- **class `QueueChainFailure`** — A terminal outcome the queue could not write into its record.
  - `const QueueChainFailure({required this.stem, required this.n, required this.phase, required this.code, required this.message})` — A failed write, retaining its item, terminal phase and failure's full message.
  - `final BatchStem stem` — The queue record that could not be written.
  - `final int n` — The item's stable number.
  - `final String phase` — The heard terminal phase: done, failed or cancelled.
  - `final String code` — The write failure's code.
  - `final String message` — The write failure's message as it came.
- **class `QueuePreparation`** — A place's preparation across the state seam, without a render UI type (§6.15).
  - `const QueuePreparation({required this.ready, this.reason, this.route = 'none', this.model, this.platform, this.cost, this.item})` — A preparation or its refusal, with an unknown cost kept null.
  - `final bool ready` — Whether its frozen item is ready to submit; on a `prepareBeforeWriting` answer, only leave to write.
  - `final String? reason` — The refusal's code, or null when ready.
  - `final String route` — `local`, `server`, `paid`, `lent`, or `none` before a route opens.
  - `final String? model` — The model where a candidate opened.
  - `final String? platform` — The opened candidate's platform.
  - `final Money? cost` — Amount and currency, or null when unknown.
  - `final Map<String, Object?>? item` — The frozen queue item as JSON, without its record number; null when refused or from `prepareBeforeWriting`.
- **class `QueueJob`** — A job a queue item became, as its row shows it: the phase, its state code, its take once done, and its actions.
  - `const QueueJob({required this.phase, this.state = '', this.take, this.actions = const []})` — A job of its parts.
  - `final String phase` — The job's phase by name: `queued`, `working`, `waiting`, `needsAttention`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`.
  - `final String state` — The job's state code, which the Activity page's sentence reads.
  - `final String? take` — The take's reference once done; null before, or where the job made none.
  - `final List<String> actions` — The codes of the actions the job offers now, as the Activity page offers them: `stop`, `dismiss`, ….
- **class `UnavailableQueueRunner`** — The runner where none is installed: every call answers *not available*.
  - `const UnavailableQueueRunner()` — The runner of a build without the render queue.

### `lib/src/script_focus.dart`

- **class `ScriptFocus`** — The block open in a scene's script editor, and who opened it.
  - `const ScriptFocus({required this.stem, required this.blockId, required this.index, required this.by})` — The block [blockId] at [index] of [stem]'s script, opened by [by].
  - `final String stem` — The scene's file stem, whose form's editor has the block open.
  - `final String? blockId` — The block's `bl_<n>`; null for a block that has none yet.
  - `final int index` — The block's place in the scene's list, 0 first.
  - `final String by` — Who opened it: `person` for the editor's own reasons, `timeline` for an opening the timeline asked.
  - `bool sameBlock(ScriptFocus other)` — The same block of the same scene, whoever opened it: what a close must name to clear it.
- **variable** `final scriptFocusProvider` — The block the script editor has open, published by the editor after the frame that opened or condensed it.
- **class `ScriptFocusController`** — Holds the block open in the script editor; the editor's two doors, [opened] and [closed], are its only writers.
  - `bool get live` — Whether its scope still stands.
  - `void opened(ScriptFocus focus)` — [focus] is the block now open.
  - `void closed(ScriptFocus focus)` — [focus] condensed: cleared only where it is the block current.
- **class `ScriptFocusRequest`** — The dock's request that the editor of [stem] open a block.
  - `const ScriptFocusRequest({required this.stem, required this.blockId, required this.index, required this.serial})` — The request numbered [serial] for the block [blockId] at [index] of [stem]'s script.
  - `final String stem` — The scene's file stem: only the editor of that scene answers.
  - `final String? blockId` — The block's `bl_<n>`, by which the request is delivered wherever the block now is; null where it has none.
  - `final int index` — The block's place when it was asked: what delivers a request with no [blockId].
  - `final int serial` — The request's number, raised by every ask.
- **variable** `final scriptFocusRequestProvider` — The last request for a block to open; the editor of its scene listens.
- **class `ScriptFocusRequests`** — Holds the last request for a block to open; [ask] is its one door.
  - `void ask(String stem, String? blockId, int index, {required String by})` — Asks the editor of [stem] to open the block at [index] ([blockId] where it has one), on behalf of [by].
- **class `TimelineCharge`** — Who is in charge of which block is open in the script, and whether the dock is being pressed.
  - `const TimelineCharge({this.following = false, this.dockPressed = false})` — The charge: the person's, with no press in the dock, unless said otherwise.
  - `final bool following` — Whether the timeline is in charge of which block is open, from a press in the dock until the person takes it back.
  - `final bool dockPressed` — Whether a pointer is down in the dock: the one press outside a block that does not condense it.
- **variable** `final timelineChargeProvider` — Who is in charge of which block is open in the script: the editor, or the timeline.
- **class `TimelineChargeController`** — Holds [TimelineCharge]; written from gestures and focus listeners only, never from a widget's lifecycle.
  - `void follow(bool on, {required String how})` — The timeline takes charge ([on]) or gives it back, [how] saying why.
  - `void dockPress(bool down)` — A pointer goes down in the dock ([down]), or up or cancelled there.

### `lib/src/script_row_text.dart`

- **class `ScriptRowText`** — What a row of the script says, wherever it is drawn — the tree's Script branch, the Script page and a folder's contents — so that the three read alike: the row's words, the page it opens and whether a reader flags it,…
  - `const ScriptRowText({required this.label, this.detail, this.tooltip, this.shortName, this.selection, this.hasProblem = false, this.isDeleted = false})`
  - `final String label` — Name first, as the library's rows are.
  - `final String? detail` — A folder's kind in words, a scene's short name — or the reason the row is flagged.
  - `final String? tooltip` — The stem, since the row shows the name; a longer reason for a cycle.
  - `final String? shortName` — A folder's short name, which its row shows nowhere: for a filter *by name or tag*.
  - `final Selection? selection` — The page the row opens; null for an entry that names nothing the project has.
  - `final bool hasProblem`
  - `final bool isDeleted` — The version drawn is in the recycle bin (§7): the row keeps its place, struck, with *deleted* as its detail, and opens that very version.
  - `factory ScriptRowText.of(AppLocalizations l10n, ScriptRow row)` — The words for [row].
- **function** `String? folderKindDetail(AppLocalizations l10n, Entity folder)` — A folder's kind in words: the vocabulary's in the reader's language and in lower case, as every detail of the tree is.

### `lib/src/script_view.dart`

- **enum `ScriptViewMode`** — How the Script tab of a folder or of the whole film is read: as a screenplay page, a grid of scene cards, or a timeline of the scenes by page length.
  - values: `page`, `grid`, `timeline`
- **enum `ScriptTimelineColouring`** — What the Script tab's timeline colours its scenes by: the scene grid's stripe, or a hue for each location.
  - values: `board`, `location`
- **class `ScriptViewState`** — How a reader is looking at the script of the open film: the view, and what an aggregate is narrowed to (§9.3).
  - `const ScriptViewState({ this.mode = ScriptViewMode.page, this.colouring = ScriptTimelineColouring.board, this.character = '', this.location = '', t…` — A reading in [mode] narrowed by the filters given; with none, the whole script as a page.
  - `final ScriptViewMode mode` — Whether a folder's and the whole film's script are read as a page, a grid of scene cards or a timeline.
  - `final ScriptTimelineColouring colouring` — What the timeline colours its scenes by; a way of looking like [mode], so *Clear* keeps it.
  - `final String character` — The character's tag a reader has narrowed to; empty for every character.
  - `final String location` — The location's tag a reader has narrowed to; empty for every location.
  - `final String resource` — The prop, outfit or other resource's tag a reader has narrowed to; empty for all of them.
  - `final bool interior` — Whether scenes inside are asked for: with [exterior], a pair that asks nothing where neither is chosen.
  - `final bool exterior` — Whether scenes outside are asked for: with [interior], a pair that asks for either where both are chosen.
  - `final bool day` — Whether scenes by day are asked for — any time not plainly night: with [night], a pair like the other.
  - `final bool night` — Whether scenes at night are asked for, by the words a slug line uses for it: with [day], a pair like the other.
  - `final String search` — Words that must appear among the words the page draws for a scene; empty for every scene.
  - `bool get isFiltered` — Whether anything at all narrows what is shown.
  - `Object get filters` — The filters as one value, equal where they narrow alike, the mode and the colouring left out.
  - `Map<String, Object?> get logged` — The filters as the log records them; the search's words are logged only once a search settles (§9.3).
  - `static List<String> resourcesOf(Entity scene)` — The props, outfits and resources [scene] names, by tag: an entry is a tag or a map naming its tag (`{"prop": "chart", "epoch": "default"}`, Project Specification §10).
  - `Map<String, Object?>? failure(Entity scene, SceneCard card, String words)` — Why [scene] is not shown under these filters, null where it is: the first filter that failed and what it compared.
  - `ScriptViewState copyWith({ ScriptViewMode? mode, ScriptTimelineColouring? colouring, String? character, String? location, String? resource, bool? i…` — This reading with the values given changed and the rest kept.
- **class `ScriptViewController`** — The view and filters the Script tab is read with, kept across the tree and reset when another film opens (§9.3).
  - `void setMode(ScriptViewMode mode)` — Shows the script the other way, keeping whatever it is narrowed to.
  - `void setColouring(ScriptTimelineColouring colouring)` — Colours the timeline's scenes another way, keeping the view and whatever the script is narrowed to.
  - `void setCharacter(String tag)` — Narrows to one character, or to every character where [tag] is empty.
  - `void setLocation(String tag)` — Narrows to one location, or to every location where [tag] is empty.
  - `void setResource(String tag)` — Narrows to one prop, outfit or resource, or to all of them where [tag] is empty.
  - `void setSearch(String words)` — Narrows to scenes whose drawn words hold [words]; empty shows every scene.
  - `void toggleInterior()` — Turns the interior chip on or off.
  - `void toggleExterior()` — Turns the exterior chip on or off.
  - `void toggleDay()` — Turns the day chip on or off.
  - `void toggleNight()` — Turns the night chip on or off.
  - `void clear()` — Shows everything again, keeping the view and the colouring the reader chose.
- **variable** `final scriptViewProvider` — How the open film's script is being read: the view and its filters (§9.3).
